newsitem.title: FRANCE: Minor fire put out in Channel Tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Minor fire put out in Channel Tunnel.

text.p: A small fire broke out in the Channel Tunnel on Wednesday near the site of a blaze on a freight train last week but was quickly extinguished without casualties, Anglo-French operator Eurotunnel SA Plc said.
Sparks caused by a blow-torch during welding repairs on the damaged section of the tunnel triggered the fire.
"Ten litres (two gallons) of water were sufficient to put out this fire," said Francois Borel, a spokesman for Eurotunnel.

"This type of situation has already happened several times in recent days. It was sparks from welding equipment used by workers working on repairs in the tunnel," he said, confirming reports by British police.
British fire fighters were alerted after the fire.
"There was an extremely minor fire in the same site as the previous fire. From what I understand, Eurotunnel had their own fire personnel there, so they dealt with it," a Kent police spokesman said.

The fire came as the company sought to reassure the public about the safety of the Tunnel after last week's fire, on a train carrying trucks and 34 passengers and crew. Eight were taken to hospital after the blaze.
The fire has halted passenger rail services between France and Britain.
